# Floor Test Protocol — Managed Terminal Environment

<!-- Chunk: docs/chunks/onboarding_terminal_env - Managed participant terminal environment -->

Per `docs/trunk/TESTING_PHILOSOPHY.md` (Floor Testing): before this
environment is considered done *the first time*, at least one person
matching the audience floor (DEC-004: comfortable with everyday computer
use, **no programming or terminal experience**) works through the tasks
below while an author observes silently. Observed friction is fixed, not
explained away; findings route to `docs/trunk/FRICTION.md`.

## Preconditions

- A laptop the tester can install software on (run once per platform:
  macOS and Windows).
- The installer one-liner on a piece of paper or in an email — exactly as
  the setup guide will present it, with expected output.
- Observer says nothing after the session starts except "what are you
  thinking?" when the tester goes silent for more than ~30 seconds.

## Tasks (read to the tester verbatim)

1. "Install the course environment using these instructions." (The full
   setup-guide install path, ending with `course-check` saying PASS.)
2. "Open the course terminal." (Watch: do they find the right app? On
   Windows, do they avoid the Start-menu Git Bash icon?)
3. "Make a folder for the course, put a file in it using TextEdit/Notepad,
   and save a checkpoint of the folder." (First `commit` run: init
   explanation, identity setup, naming prompt.)
4. "Change the file, save another checkpoint."
5. "Now put the folder back the way it was at the first checkpoint."
   (`revert`: listing, numbering, confirmation.)
6. "Change the file again but do NOT checkpoint. Now try to go back to an
   earlier checkpoint." (The uncommitted-work gate: do they understand the
   three options? Does the default feel safe?)

## What the observer records

- Hesitations longer than ~10 seconds, and what was on screen.
- Words the tester misread or asked about ("checkpoint"? "set aside"?).
- Every question asked aloud, verbatim.
- Wrong guesses (clicked/typed something we didn't expect).
- Time per task.
- **Defect** = the tester could not proceed without help, or proceeded to
  an outcome they didn't intend. **Observation** = friction that didn't
  block. Both get logged; defects block cohort use until fixed.

## DEC-007 keybinding audit (technical, same session or separate)

With pi running in the installed environment:

- **Windows (stable Windows Terminal 1.24)**: walk pi's full default
  keybinding list (`/hotkeys`; pi docs/keybindings.md). Shift+Enter and
  Alt+Enter are covered by the sendInput patch; record every *other* chord
  that fails to disambiguate, so the setup guide can warn or remap.
- **macOS (Ghostty)**: verify Option+Enter queues a follow-up with the
  installed `macos-option-as-alt = true`; then remove that line and record
  whether it still works (research §4 caveat 3). Verify Shift+Enter
  newline, Escape abort, Ctrl+O / Ctrl+T toggles.

## Results log

### Automated checks (run 2026-08-02, macOS 15 / Darwin 25.5.0)

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `env/tests/test-commands.sh` — commit/revert end-to-end in throwaway repos (init flow, identity, naming, no-change, $HOME refusal, restore semantics incl. deleted-file-returns and added-file-removed, restore-is-a-checkpoint, uncommitted-work gate all 3 options, set-aside confirmation word, cancel paths, no-repo message) | **43/43 PASS** |
| `env/tests/test-install.sh` — install.sh --skip-packages against temp HOME (install root, bash_profile/zshrc/Ghostty managed blocks, backups, idempotent re-run, user-content preservation, legacy shift+enter removal, .bashrc-not-shadowed, PATH via login bash, uninstall clean) | **35/35 PASS** |
| `docs/chunks/onboarding_terminal_env/wt-patch-parity.js` — Windows Terminal settings.json transformation logic against fixtures (sendInput actions, tag-based replace not duplicate, WT alt+enter fullscreen removal, legacy keybindings removal, Git Bash profile + defaultProfile, old-schema wrapping, idempotency, empty-settings case) | **20/20 PASS** |

`bash -n` clean on all shell scripts; `--help`/`--version` exercised on all
three commands. The Ghostty config generated by `install.sh
--skip-packages` passes `ghostty +validate-config` (run 2026-08-02 against
the ghostty 1.x binary available on the authoring machine).
